Ministers

BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Pakistan's Foreign
Ministers met in Islamabad on the 13th
January, 2007 and also at New Delhi and
discussed a number of issues and signed a

Government quarters
*142. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will
the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the residents in types II
and III Government houses in Delhi have
demanded modification of window designs
to facilitate installation of air conditioners
to meet the onslaught of summer season
and to fight the breeding of dengue
mosquitoes in desert coolers;
(b) whether window design change has
been denied on the ground that installation
of air conditioners would involve increase
in load sanctioned for the quarter; and
(c) the number of quarters that have
installed air conditioners in the windows
or by making opening in the walls?
Proposals for NHs from UP
†*143. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:

(a) whether any proposal for
upgradation, development and improvement
of National Highways has been received by
Government from the State Government of

Fifth phase of NHDP
*144. SHRI DEVDAS APTE: Will the
Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Cabinet
Committee on Economic Affairs had given
its approval to the fifth phase of the
National Highway Development
Programme (NHDP);

same; and
(d) the sectors of the road development

Development of residential property
in Delhi

SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
 Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any policy to allow the private
sector to acquire land to develop residential
properties in the National Capital;

Creation of Ombudsman in IT
*146. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether telecommunication sector
does not have the Ombudsman System;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whehter it is proposed to put
Ombudsman System in place;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
OBC candidates in general list
*147. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the number of candidates belonging
to OBC category who have been selected
in All India Civil Services Examination
during the last five years;
(b) the number out of these candidates
selected on the basis of their merit in the
general list during that period;
(c) whether it is a fact that the candidates
selected on merit in general category are
also shown as part of OBC category; and
(d) if so, what are the reasons
therefor?

Four lanes on NH 203
*148. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to construct
four lanes on NH 203 from Bhubaneswar
to Puri;
(b) if so, the status of the project; and
(c) the time-frame within which it would
be started and completed?
Unwanted commercial messages
*149. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
all private telecom companies entertain
complaints and redressal of grievance and
requests like stopping of unwanted
commercial messages only if they are made
'Online' through the internet;
(b) if so, whether Government have
made any effort to direct, induce, promote
or advise all private telecom operators to
have at least one fixed office for every lakh
subscribers;
(c) the reasons for Government ignoring
the constant harassment of subscribers
who are being bombarded with hundreds
of unwanted commercial messages every
day and night; and
(d) the steps proposed to stop this
harassment of millions of people?
Second Administrative Reforms
Commission
  †*150. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
  SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have received
the Second Administrative Reforms
Commission Report;
(b) if so, the salient recommendations
of the Commission;
(c) whether Government have taken any
decision with regard to the implementation
of these recommendations; and
(d) if so, the facts in this regard?
Delinking of CMPDIL from CIL
  *151. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to refer to the answer to Unstarred Question
1024 given in Rajya Sabha on the 3rd
August, 2006 and state:
(a) whether Government are considering
the proposal to separate Central Mine
Planning and Design Institute Ltd.
(CMPDIL) from Coal India as per the
recommendations of Shankar Committee
Report;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the employees of Coal India
Limited and CMPDIL have opposed the
proposal; and
(d) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to discuss it with trade
unions?

49
Shortage of housing in NER
*152. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of
HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY
ALLEVIA-TION be pleased to state:
(a) whether any study has been carried
out by Government on shortage of housing
units in the North Eastern Region,
especially in Assam;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government propose to
make up for the shortage by constructing
housing units, more particularly in Assam;
and
(d) if so, by when?
Dredging operations for Southern
Naval Command
*153. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
          SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that dredging
operations for Southern Naval Command
in Kochi is being carried out by Cochin
Port Trust;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether this operation is adding to
the operating cost of Cochin Port Trust;
(d) if so, the extent thereof; and
(e) whether Cochin Port Trust has
taken up the issue with the Ministry of
Defence to share the cost so as to reduce
its operating cost?
Dam on Brahmaputra river
*154. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
  SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether India has expressed concern
over China's reported plan to build a dam
on the Brahmaputra river and divert 200
billion cubic meters of water annually to
feed its ageing Yellow river;
(b) whether this issue and security
concerns over investments by Chinese
companies and settlement of border issues
were discussed with Chinese President
during his recent visit to India;
(c) if so, the other issues discussed; and
(d) whether any concrete agreements
were reached and signed?
Generation of electricity from nuclear
power
*155. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the percentage of electricity
generated from nuclear power in the country
is much lower than that of developed
countries like US, Japan, Germany, etc.;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor; and
(c) the efforts made by Government to
augment generation of electricity from
nuclear power?
Revision of telephone tariffs
*156. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:

50

other telephone charges have been revised
and reduced;
(b) if so, to what extent;
(c) the details of the original and revised
tariffs; and
(d) the circumstances and rationale for
the revision?
PoWs languishing in Pakistani jails
*157. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any formal proposal from Pakistan as a
follow up of recent offer by the President
of that country regarding the search
of Indian PoWs languishing in Pakistani
jails;
(b) if not, whether Government have
followed it up with Government of Pakistan;
(c) if so, whether Government have
formulated the modalities;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor and by
when the modalities are likely to be finalised?
Indian passports in circulation
*158. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Indian passports in
circulation in the country;
(b) the number of passport offices in
the country and their grade;
(c) whether Government propose to
issue electronic passports;
(d) whether such passports are already
issued; and
(e) if not, by when such passports are
proposed to be issued?
Court of Enquiry for Bhatdih Colliery
*159. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
  SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the statutory Court of
Enquiry for Bhatdih Colliery (Nagda
Section of BCCL) accident on 6th
September, 2006 has been constituted;
(b) whether non-judicial personnel are
included in the Court of Enquiry;
(c) whether normally sitting or retired
Judges of High Courts/Supreme Court are
appointed by Government for the
chairmanship of such Statutory
Committees;
(d) if so, the reasons for nominating
non-judicial personnel in this Court of
Enquiry;
(e) whether the trade unions have raised
objection on appointment of non-judicial
personnel; and
(f) if so, the steps taken by Government
in this regard?

Setting up an atomic energy plant at
Banswara, Rajasthan
†1022. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government would
consider to set up four units of one
thousand Mega Watt each at Raughat in
Karauli district besides setting-up an atomic
energy plant at Banswara in Rajasthan so
that dacoit affected areas of Rajasthan,
Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh could
be developed; and
(b) whether this energy could be used
in electrification of the railways so that
diesel energy is saved and its import could
be reduced?
Mining of Uranium in Meghalaya by
UCIL
†1023. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Uranium Corporation of
India Limited is going to start mining of
Uranium in Meghalaya;
(b) if so, the quantity likely to be mined
annually;
(c) whether Uranium is also available in
other parts of the country besides
Meghalaya; and
(d) if so, by when the mining process
would be started?
Titanium deposits in the country
1024. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
large deposits of Titanium in our country;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating
details of projects undertaken, if any, for
commercial harnessing of Titanium
deposits;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

238
(c) whether Government are
contemplating augmented harnessing of the
Titanium in the country;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) if not, the reasons therefor;
(f) the details of proposals, if any,
received from overseas enterprises in this
regard indicating those rejected, accepted
and under-consideration presently; and
(g) the reasons in the cases of rejections

Rehabilitation package to people
residing near mines
1025. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Uranium
mining is hazardous to the people residing
near mines;
(b) if so, the details thereof regarding
the proposed Uranium extracted places; and
(c) whether there is any rehabilitation
package available to the people residing near
Nallagonda in Andhra Pradesh?
Tailing ponds of UCIL
1026. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Uranium
Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) tailing
ponds are health risk for the villagers of
adjoining areas;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the remedial steps Government are
taking in this regard?
Supply of Uranium for Nuclear Power
Plants
1027. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) in view of the situation arising out
of non-availability of urea due to depending
on high cost Imported urea, whether
Government have visualized the similar
scenario may emerge in power sector, also
if the country depends on the imported
Uranium for running nuclear power plants
as the international cost of Uranium may
go high, leading to escalation in cost of
power; and
(b) if so, the steps Government propose
to meet the impending situation thereof?
Allocation of coal blocks for captive
coal mining
1028. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Ministry plans to allocate
38 coal blocks for captive coal mining with
the total coal reserves of 62,907.078 million
tonnes situated in Jharkhand, West Bengal,
Orissa, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and
Chhattisgarh to the power, iron, steel and
cement sectors by 2007;
(b) whether his Ministry has asked the
interested companies to file their
applications by January 12, 2007 and
registered under the Indian Companies Act,
1956 for the allocation of one or more coal
blocks of the 38 blocks; and
(c) if so, by when they are likely to be
allocated these blocks?

Different rates for selling of coal
†1029. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that different
rates for the sale of coal are fixed in the
country;
(b) if so, whether subsidy is also
provided at the time of fixing such rates;
(c) the different rates for sale of coal
during the years 2005-06 and 2006-07;
(d) the amount of subsidy provided for
sale of coal during each year of the said
period; and
(e) the consumers to whom subsidised
coal is provided?
Illegal mining in various States
1030. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that illegal coal
mining has been going on unchecked in areas
touching West Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand
like Asansol and has caused cracks in the
highways;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) the quantity of coal extracted illegally
during the last three years and the
responsibility fixed on those who failed to
check this illegal mining; and
(d) the steps taken to stop this illegal
mining?
Relocation of Jharia city, Jharkhand
†1031. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any draft scheme from the State
Government regarding relocation of Jharia
city of Jharkhand to another place, which
is facing the problem of underground fire in
coal mines;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the view point of Government in
this regard?
Acquisition of foreign coal mines
†1032. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to set up a special company for acquisition
of foreign coal mines;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) Government's policy in this regard?
Black marketing of coal in Jharkhand
1033. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the amount of coal which is excavated
by black marketeers and sold in the open
market in the State of Jharkhand;
(b) whether it is a fact that trucks with
forged documents carry coal all over the
country in connivance with district and
State administration;
(c) whether Government propose to
stop this practice altogether; and
(d) if so, the mechanisms Government
would propose to adopt to stop illegal coal
mining and trading thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Import of coal
†1034. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of coal reserves in the
country;
(b) the quantity of coal that has been
mined from these reserves;
(c) whether it is a fact that coal is being
imported despite coal reserves in
abundance; and
(d) the efforts being made by
Government for increasing the mining
capacity of coal companies so that the
country achieves self-sufficiency in this
field?
Opening of new coal mines
1035. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to open new coal mines in various parts of
the country to increase coal production;
(b) whether Government also propose
to hand over certain new coal mines to the
private sector;
(c) if so, the details thereof, location-
wise and company-wise; and
(d) the total investment required for the
purpose and the time by which new coal
mines are likely to commence production?
Amendment of Coal Mines
(Nationalisation) Act
†1036. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether any proposal to amend the
Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act with a
view to attract investment through private
participation in the field of coal mining is
under consideration;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the major requirement of
power in the country is being met through
the coal sector; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
further steps being taken to meet the
requirement of coal?
SPV for buying coal blocks abroad
1037. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Coal India Ltd. (CIL)
proposes to set up two Special Purpose
Vehicles (SPVs) to buy coal blocks abroad;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether this unit also proposes to
increase the coal production to 520 ml.
tonnes per year during the Eleventh Five
Year Plan; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Corruption in coal companies
1038. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there is rampant corruption
and irregularities in coal companies which
Government have failed to check; and
(b) the steps taken to check the
corruption and irregularities in coal
companies?
Accidents in coal mines
†1039. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether there have been many
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

accidents in coal mines during the last four
to five years;
(b) if so, the number of such accidents
occurred so far;
(c) the number of people killed so far in
such accidents; and
(d) the details of assistance provided
by Government to the next of kin of the
deceased?
Policy on 3G spectrum
1040. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had appointed
a Committee consisting of Group of
Ministers (GoM) to recommend the
vacation plan for spectrum from
Government and semi-Government agencies
such as defence, space and paramilitary, etc.;
(b) if so, the main recommendations
thereof; and
(c) by when the DoT would finalize the
policy on 3G spectrum?
Investment in broadband
infrastructure by BSNL
1041. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the State-
owned telecom major Bharat Sanchar Nigam
Ltd. has decided to invest about Rs. 2,000
crore to augment its broadband
infrastructure in urban and rural areas across
the country;
(b) whether the company recently
announced that it would upgrade its existing
broadband subscribers getting 256 kbps
speed to 2 mbs at the existing tariff of
Rs. 250 a month;
(c) whether at present BSNL has 8.2
lakh subscribers using the 256 kbps
broadband connection across the country;
and
(d) whether BSNL is also gearing up to
deploy Wi-Max in the rural areas where it
is difficult to offer broadband connection
over copper lines?
IT exports and imports by India
1042. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that IT exports
worth sixty billion dollars are expected by
the year 2010;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the countries which are importing
IT products from India and the level of
their imports; and
(d) the current level of import of software
and hardware and likely import by 2010?
Speed Post centres in Assam
1043. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of Speed Post centres in
Assam, district-wise and city-wise;

242
(b) whether Government are likely to
spread this facility in rural areas of Assam;
and
(c) if so, the number of such centres
which would be opened in the first instance?
Unique Identification Number to
every citizen
1044. SHRI P.R. RAJAN: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Department of
Information Technology is going to assign
a Unique Identification Number to every
citizen of the country; and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the
details of the project?
Offers made by MTNL
1045. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of offers MTNL has
recently made to subscribers on the
occasion of Diwali festival and afterwards;
(b) the impact each of these offers have
made on the subscribers;
(c) whether it is a fact that the impact
of these offers has been negligible; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Stagnation of rural tele-density
1046. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether rural telephony is not
catching up as targeted, resulting in rural
tele-density stagnating around 2 per cent
against a projected 25 per cent by 2010;
(b) whether adequate funds accrue from
Universal Service Obligation levy for rural
telephony expansion;
(c) whether it is a fact that private
telecom operators are defaulting on rural
telephony sector obligations; and
(d) if so, the steps being taken to ensure
compliance by private telecom operators?
Making post offices technology savvy
1047. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
spruce up post offices and make them
technology savvy to attract more investors;
(b) if so, the steps taken and
programmes initiated in detail during the
last three years, year-wise, State-wise and
category-wise;
(c) if so, the details of the steps taken
and programmes formulated and
implemented to augment savings and
investment potential of post office for the
last three years, year-wise, State-wise; and
(d) the details of the steps taken to
generate new revenue streams and
employment generated through post offices
for the last three years, year-wise,
category-wise?
Expansion of BSNL's subscribers
